summary.text: Paul Gosar is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 9th Congressional District. A dentist who ran a practice in Flagstaff, he was first elected to the House in 2010 with no prior political experience and is serving his seventh term. He serves on the Natural Resources and Oversight and Government Reform committees.

paragraphs.text: Gosar was born in Rock Springs, Wyoming, on November 27, 1958, and was raised in Pinedale, Wyoming, where he graduated from Pinedale High School in 1977.
He earned a B.S. from Creighton University in 1981 and a D.D.S. from the university in 1985.

Gosar worked as a dentist, and his official bio says he owned his dental practice and was a small businessman in Flagstaff for 25 years before his election to Congress. Wikipedia lists his Flagstaff practice as running from 1989 to 2010, and says he served as president of the Arizona Dental Association from 2004 to 2005.

Gosar was first elected to the U.S. House in 2010 as a practicing dentist with no prior political experience, defeating incumbent Rep. Ann Kirkpatrick in the 1st District, and he is now in his seventh term. He moved to the newly created 4th District in 2012 and has represented the redrawn 9th District since 2023.

He serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. He previously chaired the Congressional Western Caucus in the 115th and 116th Congresses.

On November 17, 2021, the House voted 223-207 to censure Gosar and remove him from his committee assignments over a video he posted depicting violence toward Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. He said the action was an attack on his First Amendment right to speak out against illegal immigration and said he does not espouse violence.
He won re-election in 2024 with 65.3% of the vote over Democrat Quacy Smith, and he advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 79,336 votes.
